options.text: A new or improved technology that builds on earlier ideas
A technology that never changes once it is built
A material that is dug out of the ground
A copy of an older tool with no changes

items.explanation: An innovation is a new or improved idea, method, or product. Innovations almost always build on the technologies that came before them.

items.stem: Engineers improve a light bulb by testing a version, finding its weak points, and redesigning it, over and over. This repeating process is called
items.explanation: Iteration is repeating a design cycle of testing and redesigning. Each loop produces a slightly better version of the technology.

items.stem: Which of these is the first step in the iteration cycle?

options.text: Repeating the cycle forever with no changes
Identifying the problem with the current design

items.explanation: The cycle starts by identifying the problem. Engineers name the weakness before they design and test a solution.

items.stem: A water treatment plant is built to give a city clean, safe drinking water. The clean water is an example of
items.explanation: An intended consequence is a result the technology was designed to produce. Clean water is exactly what the treatment plant was built to create.

items.stem: Making and throwing away millions of devices creates electronic waste. This is best described as
items.explanation: Electronic waste is a side effect no one planned, so it is an unintended consequence, even when the device works as designed.

items.stem: What does it mean for a technology to be sustainable?

options.text: It meets today's needs without using up resources future generations will need
It is the cheapest possible option to buy
It uses as many resources as possible
It can never be changed or improved

items.explanation: Sustainability means meeting present needs while protecting the resources future generations will rely on, by using resources carefully and creating less waste.

items.stem: Sunlight and wind are examples of
items.explanation: Renewable resources are replaced by nature quickly. Sunlight and wind keep returning, unlike oil or coal, which do not come back in a human lifetime.

items.stem: An LED bulb makes the same brightness as an incandescent bulb but uses about a tenth of the energy. The LED is more
items.explanation: Efficiency is how much useful work a technology does for the energy it uses. Doing the same job with far less energy makes the LED more efficient.

items.stem: An LED bulb costs more to buy than an old bulb, but it lasts for years and saves energy. Choosing it means weighing cost against savings. This kind of give-and-take is a
items.explanation: A trade-off means gaining one benefit by giving up another. Engineers weigh the higher upfront cost against the long-term energy savings and lower impact.

items.stem: When engineers evaluate a sustainable design, which of these do they need to balance?

options.text: Only the cost of the materials
Only how fast it can be built
Human needs, cost, resources, and environmental impact together
Only the color of the product

items.explanation: Good design balances many factors at once: human needs, cost, available resources, environmental impact, and the needs of future generations.
